objective: Coordinator's go-ahead (18 November 2026) on RING-READ-20261118-001's direction 1. Run the incremental reader R3 (RING-READ-20261118-001B, frozen) on every stage, to a fixed cap, of all 26,441 TOUCH-CENSUS-20261118-001 arrangements under the cheapest counts, and on the 247 mixed-count stages of FRESH-COUNT-20261118-001 whose threshold reader misread 47. Ask what is typical: how many stages read exactly, what the misreads share, and whether the distance the reader needs is set by the largest junction (largest size less one) across the census, against VARIABLE-OUTPUT-READER-20261118-001H's fixed cutoff of five. Stop at the census read or a class of misreads explained. Serves G1, G17 and A97.
status: Complete 2026-11-19 (Partially successful; referee pending): across all 26,441 cheapest-count census arrangements (100,024 stages on exact tables) the ring's distance reader, made name-free, reads 2,353 stages exactly. Three causes stop it: 92% of starts have knots sharing two distinctions (93,808 stages, 3 exact); stages that are not rigid; and tables whose symmetries move a junction (0 of 1,480 read, as no table-only reader can). Where junctions meet once it reads 38%; where no table symmetry moves a junction, 68% of 1,944 small stages. On every stage it reads, the distance needed is the largest junction less one (largest 3 to 9).
stop_rule: The census and the mixed stages read, misreads classified; referee hand-off; report.
title: Does the new distance reader read every growing census arrangement?
